newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Dollar falls below 1.7 marks, Euro stocks slip.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Dollar falls below 1.7 marks, Euro stocks slip.

text.p: The dollar slipped from early highs against the mark reached on a uncertainty about China, while European stock markets also ran out of steam as Wall Street set no clear trend.
Fears about the health of paramount Chinese leader Deng Xiaoping and trouble in the Middle East kept the dollar firm against the mark in early trade.
At one point, the dollar hit a 34-month record of 1.7050 marks. But it could not hold at such heights and slipped to 1.6973 marks by mid afternoon, just below Monday's European close of 1.6997.
News that Chinese leaders were hurriedly returning to Beijing fuelled fears that 93-year-old Deng, the father of China's economic reform, might be seriously ill.

The Foreign Ministry said there had been no change in his health but the prospect of instability in China was reason enough to buy dollars, along with news of a skirmish between Iranian forces and an opposition groups based in Iraq.

But these factors wore off over the day despite support for a robust dollar from French Finance Minister Jean Arthuis. "I would like a strong dollar, but even more a robust dollar ... for this exchange rate to be lasting," he told parliament.
Against the yen, the dollar was muted due to lingering worries of Bank of Japan intervention after the dollar's surge. It fell to 124.12 yen from 124.50 at Monday's close.

Interest rates jitters began to emerge again although U.S. Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan is not due to give his Humphrey-Hawkins testimony to Congress until February 27. "I think the markets are going to get increasingly nervous the closer we get to that Greenspan speech," one trader said.

Much of the action on currency markets was on the lira, which tumbled amid concern that Italy might not make the first wave of European economic and monetary union (EMU). The lira fell to 993.30 to the mark from 987.25 late on Monday.

Dealers blamed comments from Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi and Belgian central bank chief Alfonse Verplaetse. Prodi said on Monday that Germany was less committed to EMU than Italy, fuelling rumours that Bonn was conspiring to keep the lira out of the first wave of nations joining the European currency's launch.
Verplaetse also made comments apparently questioning the lira's ability to join EMU early, although he later denied he had been referring to Italy.

"This is building up into a bit of a row between Italy and Germany and all the underlying tensions are gradually coming to the surface," said David Coleman, Chief Economist at CIBC Wood Gundy. He said the market would closely watch a speech on the euro by German Secretary of State for Finance Juergen Stark at 1645 GMT for any mention of the lira.
On equity markets, the long wait for guidance from Wall Street after Monday's U.S. holiday proved fruitless.
Wall Street opened firmer, fell and then recovered. By mid afternoon in Europe, the Dow Jones Industrial average was up 10 points at 6,998.96.

Earlier in the day continental European bourses celebrated the dollar's strength at the time and Germany's DAX index closed up 43.59 points, or 1.35 percent, at a record 3,276.16. "The dollar is still the engine for the gains," said one Frankfurt dealer.
But in after-hours electronic trading a feeling that the market needed to consolidate after this year's bull run gained strength and the IBIS index was down 4.64 points at 3,255.66.
France's CAC-40 index likewise fell after a powerful start, and was down 7.45 points at 2,627.03 by mid afternoon.
London's FTSE 100 index was less enthusiastic than its continental counterparts throughout the day, although it did stay marginally higher. By mid afternoon it was up just 0.8 of a point at 4,338.6.

However, one uncertainty disappeared, for the time being at least, when the Conservative government survived a parliamentary censure motion on Monday night which could have led to a confidence vote and an early election.
CURRENCIES AT 1500 GMT
The dollar was quoted at 1.6973 marks and 124.12 yen compared with 1.6997 marks and 124.50 yen in late European trading on Monday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1530 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was up 0.8 points at 4,338.6.
PARIS - The CAC-40 was down 7.45 at 2,627.03 points.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index closed 43.59 points higher at a record 3,276.16.
PRECIOUS METALS AT 1530 GMT
Gold was fixed in the afternoon at $345.00 an ounce from the morning fixing of $346.00 and Monday's closing at $344.25. Silver was unchanged at $5.21.
